questions.question: What color are the road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines are painted down the center of roads. They separate lanes where traffic moves in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells you that a divided highway is coming up.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles using this emblem travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective thing you can do to protect yourself from death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What documents must you give to an officer if stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check?
questions.explanation: When stopped, you must provide your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You are required to carry all three documents when driving.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a distraction that can cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community service group is picking up trash along the highway ahead.
Workers are on or very close to the road in the work zone ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or very close to the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or near the roadway ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones on highways. They are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols and warn that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either.
It harms judgment but not driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and reduces your ability to see clearly. It also impairs your judgment about speed and distance, lowers your inhibitions, and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: May pass a slow-moving vehicle if you can do so quickly.
May pass if you know the road ahead.
May pass, but only at night.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white and rectangular with black markings. You must obey all regulatory signs. This sign means passing is not allowed.

questions.question: What are signs called that require drivers to obey an instruction?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. If you do not obey them, you can be fined.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so you cannot see as clearly as during the day. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people or vehicles are not visible from 500 feet away.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for all vehicles and pedestrians to pass before you go.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: After an accident, you must stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: When can you pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk?

options.text: When the vehicle does not move quickly after the pedestrian leaves.
When the pedestrian is directly in front of the vehicle.
When you do not see a pedestrian.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk. You must assume that any stopped vehicle at a crosswalk is waiting for a pedestrian, even if you cannot see one.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign means yield. Slow down when you see this sign at an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other drivers or pedestrians go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should you pay extra attention to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are difficult to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are hard to spot because they are smaller than cars. They may move faster and have less noticeable lights. Always look carefully for these road users to prevent crashes.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Follow what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if construction is not happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: You must slow down and follow directions from flaggers in construction zones. Not following a flagger's instructions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: Your chances of being in a crash increase after consuming:
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink increases your chance of a crash. You cannot drink alcohol and drive safely, no matter how long you have been driving.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the steering wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When you turn right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: A flashing red light works the same as what?
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red light, you must stop and let all other traffic go first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: When should you slow down when using a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Before you enter the exit ramp.
After you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down before you enter the exit ramp. Slow down only after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, when can you proceed?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks.
questions.explanation: At a crossing with more than one track, do not move when a train passes. Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks. Even at a single-track crossing, check again for another train before you cross.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Do not leave the scene without giving your information and helping if needed.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
Slow down to check if traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in each direction, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can see oncoming traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see oncoming traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: With no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the nearest point where you can see oncoming traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: When crossing signals flash at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like a lowered gate or an oncoming train.

questions.question: When is it okay to drive in a lane marked with a red X?

options.text: If there is no oncoming traffic.
If you are passing the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: Lane signals show which lanes are open or closed. A red X means the lane is closed. Never drive in a lane with a red X.
